method_note: Text was retrieved with the WebFetch tool, which returns a model-mediated extract rather than raw bytes. Locators and short excerpts below are as relayed by that tool. Page numbers are inferred from page markers and may be off by one. No excerpt has been compared against the PDF by a person, so human_verified is false for every claim. Excerpts are capped at 15 words.

status_definitions.SOURCE_TEXT_READ: Full text (or a stated character range of it) was retrieved and the claim was located in it with a section/table/figure reference. Not human verified.
status_definitions.UNVERIFIED_ABSTRACT_ONLY: Only an abstract or bibliographic record was accessible. The claim restates the abstract. Full-text location of the claim is unknown. Per protocol this is UNVERIFIED.
status_definitions.UNVERIFIED_NOT_LOCATED: No retrievable record or text was found. No claim was extracted.

claims.claim: In the study's comparison of ML models for forecasting greenhouse air temperature and relative humidity, LSTM outperformed SVMR and MLP. For LSTM the abstract reports temperature RMSE 0.352 degC with R2 0.982, and relative humidity RMSE 1.23 % with R2 0.954.

scope.crop_or_system: semi-closed greenhouse (as stated); crop not stated

claims.applicability: Shows that a forecasting method has been reported for a semi-closed greenhouse. Does not specify sensors, placement, sampling interval or training data, so it cannot define a sensing or control specification for the case.
claims.limitations: Abstract only. Training data period, sensor set, validation split and site are not stated. Accuracy is for that greenhouse and dataset and may not transfer.

claims.claim: The abstract reports cooling demand of 6.03 MWh for a two-day winter period and 15.33 MWh for a two-day summer period, and water demand of 5.85 m3 (winter) and 12.48 m3 (summer), from an analytical model driven by the LSTM forecasts.

scope.crop_or_system: semi-closed greenhouse; floor area not stated
scope.time: two-day winter and two-day summer periods; dates not stated

claims.applicability: Order-of-magnitude illustration of modelled cooling and water demand for one greenhouse. Not usable to size cooling plant, electrical supply or water supply for the case.
claims.limitations: Floor area is not stated, so values cannot be normalised per m2 or compared with S7. Whether MWh is thermal or electrical is not stated. Do not convert to AC kW.

claims.claim: A CFD model of an evaporative cooled greenhouse in Qatar, compared with measured inner air temperature, relative humidity and global solar radiation, showed that raising ventilation from 20 to 40 air changes per hour lowered average inner air temperature and reduced the temperature rise under high solar radiation.
claims.underlying_basis: MODELED (CFD) with reported agreement to measurements

scope.location: Qatar (greenhouse site not stated on the record)
scope.crop_or_system: ASHRAE-compliant evaporative cooled greenhouse; crop not stated

claims.applicability: Qualitative direction of effect for a Qatar evaporative cooled greenhouse. Not a required ventilation rate for the case.
claims.limitations: Abstract gives no temperature values, error metrics, geometry or radiation values. The abstract says 'good agreement' without numbers.

claims.claim: In the same CFD study, an uneven-span roof gave the lowest average inner temperature, aspect ratio had negligible effect for equal floor area and volume, and induction fans at or below crop height lowered average temperature.

values.value: fan elevation, roof shape, aspect ratio

scope.location: Qatar (site not stated on the record)

claims.applicability: Design-direction hint for roof form and fan placement. Not a structural or cover specification.
claims.limitations: No dimensions, spans, temperatures or error metrics in the abstract. Roof-shape result may not hold for a Venlo glass house. Which spans were compared is not stated.

claims.claim: The abstract reports a levelized cost of production for greenhouse tomatoes of $3.19 per kg versus $3.77 per kg for vertical farms in a Qatar case study, from a model that includes capital, operating and transport costs.

values.quantity: greenhouse tomato levelized cost of production
vertical farm levelized cost of production

claims.underlying_basis: MODELED (economic model with dynamic energy, water and CO2 models and a vehicle routing problem)

scope.crop_or_system: centralized greenhouse scenario versus decentralized vertical farms; greenhouse size and technology not stated

claims.applicability: Screening comparator only. Not a quote, a CAPEX figure or a farm-level margin for the case.
claims.limitations: Currency and base year not stated. Cost assumptions are in the full paper, which was not accessible. A modelled central-greenhouse value is not the cost of one small greenhouse.

claims.claim: In a measured tomato trial in a pad-and-fan cooled glass Venlo greenhouse in Riyadh (cultivation 24 Feb to 23 Dec 2019), pad-wall cooling water was 3190 L/m2 for the season, about 42 % less than in the tunnel greenhouse compared (5463 L/m2). Total water was 4435 L/m2, of which about 72 % was for cooling.

values.quantity: pad-wall cooling water, Venlo greenhouse, season
values.unit: L/m2 (area basis, growing vs ground, not confirmed)

values.quantity: pad-wall cooling water, tunnel greenhouse, season
total water use, Venlo greenhouse, season
share of total water used for cooling, Venlo

locator.table_figure: Fig. 4A (value read graphically per the extract)

claims.excerpt_relayed: was 42% lower in the M greenhouse
claims.underlying_basis: OBSERVED (measured trial as reported by the source)

scope.location: Estidamah research centre, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia (24.7 N, 46.7 E)
scope.crop_or_system: round tomato, hydroponic on stone wool, 5 stems/m2, high wire, drain collection

claims.applicability: GCC transfer check only. Same climate class as Qatar but a different site, humidity regime and operating strategy. Not Qatar field measurement.
claims.limitations: Single site, single season. The values 5463, 4435 and 72 % come from one extraction and only the 42 % statement was re-confirmed with an excerpt. Internal arithmetic is consistent (see test_pilot.py).

claims.claim: The Riyadh glass Venlo greenhouse was 40 m x 12 m (432 m2 growing area) with a pad wall 12 m x 3 m x 15 cm and 6 frequency-controlled cooling fans of 15,000 m3/h each. The paper reports 187.5 m3/m2/h total fan capacity, which equals 90,000 m3/h divided by 480 m2 of ground area, not by the 432 m2 growing area.

values.quantity: reported total fan capacity per area

claims.excerpt_relayed: 6 frequency-controlled fans with capacity of 15,000 m3 h-1 each
claims.underlying_basis: OBSERVED (equipment as built, as reported by the source)
claims.applicability: Reference equipment configuration for a GCC Venlo greenhouse. It is not a sizing rule for Qatar. The ground-area basis (480 m2) is a derived check by this ledger, not stated in the excerpt.
claims.limitations: Only the fan sentence was re-confirmed with a verbatim excerpt. Pad and geometry dimensions come from one extraction. Glass thickness is not recorded in this claim.

claims.claim: FAO's Mediterranean-climate guide gives design rules for fan-and-pad cooling: pad area about 1 m2 per 20-30 m2 of greenhouse area, average pad face velocity 0.75-1.5 m/s, basic airflow 120-150 m3 per m2 of greenhouse area per hour, and a maximum fan-to-pad distance of 40 m.

locator.section: Chapter 4, 'Evaporative cooling: Fan and pad cooling'

claims.excerpt_relayed: should be about 1 m2 per 20-30 m2 greenhouse area
claims.applicability: Starting-point ranges for expert review only. Not a Qatar design condition and not a fan or pad specification for the case.
claims.limitations: Mediterranean climate. Qatar summer humidity and wet-bulb conditions are not addressed. A numeric temperature drop for pad cooling was not found. Page numbers inferred. The same chapter's ventilation figure (0.06 m3/s/m2 described as about 60 ACH at 3 m mean height) was deliberately NOT used: 0.06 x 3600 / 3 = 72 ACH, so the relayed statement is internally inconsistent and needs human reading of the page.

claims.claim: FAO's table of net crop water requirements lists substrate-grown tomato at 177 mm for a September-March cycle and 276 mm for a March-July cycle, citing Gallardo et al. (2009), and reports leaching fractions of 20-40 % for substrate irrigation scheduling.

values.quantity: net crop water requirement, substrate tomato, Sept-Mar
net crop water requirement, substrate tomato, Mar-July

locator.section: Chapter 6, Table 2 and 'Irrigation scheduling of greenhouse crops grown in substrate'

claims.underlying_basis: GUIDANCE (tabulated literature values for Mediterranean greenhouses)
claims.applicability: Shows the form of a net crop water requirement. Not a Qatar irrigation volume and not usable for pump or emitter sizing.
claims.limitations: Net not gross requirement. The '(162)' value beside 177 is unexplained in the relayed text. Tsafaras irrigation water in Riyadh (about 1246 L/m2 per season, from the first extraction, not in this ledger as a claim) is about 4.5-7 times these net figures, so Mediterranean values must not be carried to Qatar.

locator.section: Clause 1.5 Approval of electrical installations; Clause 1.7 Licensed contractors; Clause 3.1

claims.excerpt_relayed: The design of an Electrical Installation must be approved by KM

scope.crop_or_system: low-voltage installations generally; 'farms' appear only in the list of covered premises (clause 1.1.1, p. 4); no greenhouse-specific clause found in the read portion

claims.applicability: Establishes that electrical design needs authority approval and licensed contractors. It does not provide any rating, cable size, breaker or protection setting for a greenhouse.
